a000.label: supported
a000.reason: The actual document explicitly states that the British constitution is not set out in any single document.

a001.label: supported
a001.reason: The actual documents jointly establish that the constitution consists of many documents and is a sum of laws and principles making up the country's body politic.

a002.label: supported
a002.reason: The actual document explicitly lists all four stated primary sources.

a003.label: supported
a003.reason: The actual document situates the terminology in the Cold War and explains its division of nations into three political and economic groups.

a004.label: supported
a004.reason: The actual document identifies every listed country, Western European nations, and their allies as representing the First World.

a005.label: supported
a005.reason: The actual document identifies the Soviet Union, China, Cuba, and their allies as representing the Second World.

a006.label: supported
a006.reason: The actual document explicitly defines Third World countries by non-alignment with either NATO or the Communist Bloc.

a007.label: supported
a007.reason: The actual document describes the frequent First World/North and Third World/South associations and explicitly supplies the stated development and affluence distinctions.

a008.label: supported
a008.reason: The actual documents identify the Easter Island statues as moai and explicitly attribute their carving to the Rapa Nui people on Easter Island.

a009.label: supported
a009.reason: The actual documents identify Rano Raraku as the main quarry, describe transport from there to perimeter platforms called ahu, and describe the destinations as ceremonial sites.

a010.label: not_supported
a010.reason: The actual documents support statues remaining at the quarry and hundreds being transported, but present wooden frames and ladders as possible methods or theories. They do not establish that hundreds actually moved using those methods.

a011.label: supported
a011.reason: The actual document explicitly identifies the golden wattle, its scientific name, its status as Australia's national flower, and its representation by gold.

a012.label: supported
a012.reason: The actual documents record the gum-tree green and wattle-gold names and explicitly state that green and gold feature on Australia's coat of arms.

a013.label: supported
a013.reason: The actual document identifies the Australian cricket team's 1899 England tour as its first use of green and gold and specifies caps and blazers for the opening Ashes match.
